user.title: Connect to SmartThings
user.description: Reuse a configured Home Assistant SmartThings connection with automatic token refresh, or provide a manual access token.

device.title: Choose a Samsung EHS heat pump
device.description: Only devices exposing Samsung EHS capabilities are listed.

token.title: Use a manual SmartThings token
token.description: Enter a SmartThings personal access token with permission to read devices. The integration only sends read-only API requests.

smartthings.title: Reuse a SmartThings connection
smartthings.description: Select a connection from the built-in SmartThings integration. It must be loaded and have access to your heat pump. It continues to manage sign-in and automatic token refresh.

error.invalid_auth: Access denied. Check your manual token or repair authentication in the selected SmartThings integration.
error.cannot_connect: Unable to use SmartThings. Check that the selected connection is loaded and working, or try again later.
error.no_devices: No compatible EHS device is accessible through this connection. When reconfiguring, the existing heat pump must be accessible.

abort.no_smartthings: First add the built-in SmartThings integration in Settings → Devices & services, then try again. Alternatively, go back and enter a manual access token.

init.title: Samsung EHS settings
init.description: Select the Shelly (or other) power sensor measuring the heat pump. Supports W or kW. This replaces Samsung instantaneous power for live COP and daily energy/COP; seven-day electricity still uses the Samsung energy counter. Clear the selection to use Samsung again. If the chosen sensor is unavailable, live power and COP remain unknown without fallback. Enable the managed dashboard to add a sidebar dashboard for this heat pump. Sensor IDs are resolved automatically. Disable it to remove only the managed dashboard. Copy its configuration to a separate dashboard for customization. To download a fresh SmartThings API status response as JSON, close this dialog and choose Download diagnostics from the integration entry’s three-dot menu.

error.own_sensor: Choose a sensor from another integration, such as Shelly, to avoid a circular dependency.
error.invalid_power_unit: The sensor must measure power in W or kW, not energy in Wh or kWh.
